claims.text: The target is a multicomponent high-entropy material initially in a solid state.
The relevant regime is the high-temperature solid-to-fluid transition.
Machine-learning potentials will be incorporated into DFT free-energy studies.
Using machine-learning potentials will improve the accuracy of DFT free-energy studies.
Using machine-learning potentials will improve the computational efficiency of DFT free-energy studies.
The proposed approach will better represent the thermodynamic effects relevant to the transition.
The proposed approach will enable treatment of both the solid and dense-fluid phases around the transition.
The intervention will improve determination of the transition temperature relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve determination of fusion enthalpy relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve determination of fusion entropy relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve determination of the volume change at the transition relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The performance of the approach may be limited by the accuracy and transferability of machine-learning potentials for multicomponent high-entropy materials.
A comparison of DFT free-energy studies with and without machine-learning potentials can test the hypothesis.
Failure to improve all listed thermodynamic determinations would falsify the hypothesis.
